observation: handle_webhook parses the payload, computes totals, writes to the database and sends the notification in one 94-line body. The HTTP concern and the billing concern are not separable here, so neither can be tested without the other.

A monetary amount is a float in process_invoice, a Decimal in apply_tax, and a formatted string by the time it reaches persist_invoice. One concept, three representations, with conversion happening implicitly at each boundary.
persist_invoice catches every exception and returns None on failure. The caller cannot distinguish 'no such invoice' from 'the database is down', so both surface to the user as an empty result.
apply_tax branches on a jurisdiction string in five places. Each new jurisdiction requires editing all five, which is why the last three commits to this file each touched the same lines.
get_connection builds the DSN by string concatenation from config values with no validation, and the fallback branch defaults to a connection with credentials embedded in the literal.
